hints.title: Global Word Frequency Uniqueness
hints.text: A word is uncommon if and only if it appears exactly once across both sentences combined.

hints.title: Sentence Concatenation
hints.text: Combine words from both input strings into a single token stream.

hints.title: Single Occurrence Filter
hints.text: Count frequencies of all words in the combined stream and return those whose count equals one.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def uncommonFromSentences(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> List[str]:
        count = Counter((s1 + " " + s2).split())
        return [w for w, c in count.items() if c == 1]
```

complexity.notes: Linear pass splitting tokens and counting frequencies.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Cross-checking each word in nested loops takes O((N+M)^2) quadratic string comparisons.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Frequency table storing words requires O(N + M) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Notice that uncommon status implies global frequency count of 1 across both sentences.
